analysis: The trial timed out after 2673.019 allocated GPU-seconds and returned no validation score. Neither improvement nor degradation versus 0.4975 or 0.5050 can be established; per-category results and diagnostic completion are unavailable. A plausible runtime bottleneck is candidate-conditioned attention across up to 24 transitions per history and 257 candidates per transition, with many small checkpointed chunks adding dispatch and backward recomputation costs. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed timeout cause. The 6500-second per-category guard exceeds the observed trial allocation and did not ensure completion within it. Future experiments should reduce scoring overhead and align runtime guards with the available trial budget while preserving causal scoring and one model per category.
code_summary: Four independently trained category-specific SASRec models use 96-dimensional embeddings and two causal Transformer blocks. A jointly trained attention branch projects candidate embeddings into queries and contextual history features into keys, pools only nonpadding positions through the supervised transition, then normalizes the sequential feature plus a projected pool gated by sigmoid(alpha), initialized with alpha=-2. Shared item embeddings, the existing g residual, learned temperature, and item bias remain. Training retains sampled-softmax cross-entropy, 256 uniform negatives, complete-training-history exclusions, and at most 24 sampled transitions per history. Training and prediction share chunked scoring with gradient checkpointing during training. The predictor strictly loads one validation-selected checkpoint per category. RNG-preserving checks cover finite scores/gradients, causality, candidate permutation, chunk equivalence, and reload parity; their completion is unconfirmed because the host reported only timeout.
